These deposits can be of four kinds.

i. Non-fixed or demand deposits (Demand Deposits / Current Account)

By these are meant such deposits deposited in a bank which their owner can withdraw from the bank whenever he wishes without giving advance notice. Common business people keep their money in banks in this way. Generally the bank pays no interest on accounts of this kind. But nowadays some banks have begun paying a nominal interest on the basis of the average balance (Average Balance).

ii. Fixed Deposits

By these are meant such sums which a person deposits in a bank for a fixed period and cannot withdraw before it. Since the bank invests such money in some business or gives it on loan, it therefore gives interest on such deposits to the depositor. It is also called a fixed account.

iii. Savings Deposits

To create in people the habit of saving money, banks receive savings deposits. In an account of this kind people keep depositing small deposits, and the bank gives interest on them. But the rate of this interest is lower than on fixed deposits. The depositor can withdraw a small sum from his account whenever he wishes, but if he withdraws a larger sum, he has to give advance notice to the bank. Such accounts are suitable for the salaried class.

iv. Profit and loss sharing deposits (Profit and Loss Sharing Deposits)

Under the Islamic banking system commercial banks have also given the public this facility that they can deposit their money in a bank on the basis of partnership in profit and loss. The bank invests this money in some lawful business, and at the end of the year distributes the profit among the depositors.

2. Giving loans (Advancing Loans)

The second work of the bank is that it lends money to the needy and collects interest on this sum. This interest is the major source of the bank’s income. In reality, the money which people deposit with the bank, the bank issues that same money as loans. The bank issues loans in the following forms:

i. Bank Loan

While issuing a loan, the bank transfers the sum into the account of the borrower. The borrower can withdraw this sum at the time of need through a cheque. In this case the bank collects interest on the whole sum, even if the borrower uses only a small sum.

ii. Bank Overdraft

In this form of loan the bank collects interest only on that sum which the borrower withdraws from the bank. The bank issues a loan of this kind only to those people whose account already exists in the bank.

(continued from p.47) … do any business, e.g. employed professionals, or such people who temporarily cannot bring their sums into use, or for some reason want to keep their wealth in cash form, deposit this sum in some bank as a trust, so that on one side that sum remains safe and on the other side some interest or profit is obtained on it. These deposits can be of four kinds.

i. Non-fixed or demand deposits (Demand Deposits / Current Account)

By these are meant such deposits deposited in a bank which their owner can withdraw from the bank whenever he wishes without giving advance notice. Common business people keep their money in banks in this way. Generally the bank pays no interest on accounts of this kind. But nowadays some banks have begun paying a nominal interest on the basis of the average balance (Average Balance).

ii. Fixed Deposits

By these are meant such sums which a person deposits in a bank for a fixed period and cannot withdraw before it. Since the bank invests such money in some business or gives it on loan, it therefore gives interest on such deposits to the depositor. It is also called a fixed account.

iii. Savings Deposits

To create in people the habit of saving money, banks receive savings deposits. In an account of this kind people keep depositing small deposits, and the bank gives interest on them. But the rate of this interest is lower than on fixed deposits. The depositor can withdraw a small sum from his account whenever he wishes, but if he withdraws a larger sum, he has to give advance notice to the bank. Such accounts are suitable for the salaried class.

iv. Profit and loss sharing deposits (Profit and Loss Sharing Deposits)

Under the Islamic banking system commercial banks have also given the public this facility that they can deposit their money in a bank on the basis of partnership in profit and loss. The bank invests this money in some lawful business, and at the end of the year distributes the profit among the depositors.

2. Giving loans (Advancing Loans)

The second work of the bank is that it lends money to the needy and collects interest on this sum. This interest is the major source of the bank’s income. In reality, the money which people deposit with the bank, the bank issues that same money as loans. The bank issues loans in the following forms:

i. Bank Loan

While issuing a loan, the bank transfers the sum into the account of the borrower. The borrower can withdraw this sum at the time of need through a cheque. In this case the bank collects interest on the whole sum, even if the borrower uses only a small sum.

ii. Bank Overdraft

In this form of loan the bank collects interest only on that sum which the borrower withdraws from the bank. The bank issues a loan of this kind only to those people whose account already exists in the bank.

بینک کا دوسرا کام یہ ہے کہ یہ ضرورت مندوں کو رقم ادھار دیتا ہے اور اس رقم پر سود وصول کرتا ہے۔ یہ سود بینک کی آمدنی کا بڑا ذریعہ ہے۔ دراصل بینک کے پاس جو لوگ رقم جمع کرواتے ہیں بینک اُسی رقم کو بطور قرض جاری کرتا ہے۔ بینک درج ذیل صورتوں میں قرض جاری کرتا ہے:

i۔ بینک قرض: Bank Loan

بینک قرض جاری کرتے وقت قرض دار کے اکاؤنٹ میں رقم منتقل کرتا ہے۔ قرض دار یہ رقم ضرورت کے وقت چیک کے ذریعے سے نکلوا سکتا ہے۔ بینک اس صورت میں ساری رقم پر سود وصول کرتا ہے، قرض دار چاہے کم رقم ہی استعمال کیوں نہ کرے۔

paras.text: Another work of the bank is discounting hundis. Its method is this: suppose a merchant buys goods from some trader and promises to pay the price after one month. The seller of goods writes a document in the name of the buyer of goods, on which this order is written that the buyer will pay this sum after one month. This document is called a hundi. The seller keeps this hundi safe with him until the fixed date, and on completion of the period shows the hundi to the buyer and collects the sum. But if the seller needs the sum before the fixed period, he gets the sum from the bank. The bank deducts some sum as interest, but on the completion of the period collects the full sum from the buyer.

iii. Discounting of hundis (Discounting Bill of Exchange)

Another work of the bank is discounting hundis. Its method is this: suppose a merchant buys goods from some trader and promises to pay the price after one month. The seller of goods writes a document in the name of the buyer of goods, on which this order is written that the buyer will pay this sum after one month. This document is called a hundi. The seller keeps this hundi safe with him until the fixed date, and on completion of the period shows the hundi to the buyer and collects the sum. But if the seller needs the sum before the fixed period, he gets the sum from the bank. The bank deducts some sum as interest, but on the completion of the period collects the full sum from the buyer.

3. Cheap medium of exchange

One work of the bank is also that it provides an easy medium of exchange, e.g. the central bank of every country issues notes, which serve as an easy medium of exchange compared with heavy coins and metals; but cheques and drafts etc. issued by the central bank make large payments with greater ease and safety.

4. Transfer of Money

The bank does the work of transferring money from one place to another. If you want to transfer sums from one city to another city or from one country to another country, the bank provides this service at cheap prices. Formerly traveller’s cheques (T.C) were used for this purpose, but nowadays with the help of the internet online transfer has become even easier.

5. Investment

The bank buys the shares (Shares) of many companies and government securities. On shares the bank earns profit, whereas on securities interest is obtained. This sum becomes a major source of the bank’s income.

6. Custodian of valuables (Cutodian of Valuables)

The bank provides the facility of lockers, where people keep safe their valuable documents, e.g. wills, property registries, and other valuable things, e.g. jewellery and prize bonds etc. In return the bank collects nominal charges.

7. Services as an agent

The bank works as an agent for its customers, e.g. on their behalf it pays rent, tax and insurance instalments etc., and on the other side transfers sums being received into their accounts, like transferring sums of electricity, gas and water bills etc. into the accounts of the concerned departments.

8. Miscellaneous Functions

i. Dealing in foreign currency

ii. Advice to importers and exporters

iii. Receiving Hajj applications

iv. Information about trade conditions, etc.

بینک کا ایک کام یہ بھی ہے کہ آسان آلہ مبادلہ مہیا کرتا ہے، مثلاً ہر ملک کا مرکزی بینک نوٹ جاری کرتا ہے جو بھاری سکوں اور دھاتوں کے مقابلہ میں آسان آلہ مبادلہ کا کام دیتے ہیں لیکن مرکزی بینک کے جاری کیے ہوئے چیک اور ڈرافٹ وغیرہ کی مدد سے بڑی بڑی ادائیگیاں مزید آسانی اور حفاظت کے ساتھ کی جاتی ہیں۔

4۔ زر منتقل کرنا: Transfer of Money

بینک روپے کو ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ منتقل کرنے کا کام کرتا ہے اگر آپ ایک شہر سے دوسرے شہر یا ایک ملک سے دوسرے ملک رقوم منتقل کرنا چاہیں تو بینک یہ فریضہ سستے داموں مہیا کرتا ہے۔ پہلے اس مقصد کے لیے ٹریولرز چیک (T.C) استعمال ہوتے تھے لیکن آج کل انٹرنیٹ کی مدد سے آن لائن ٹرانسفر مزید آسان ہو گئی ہے۔

5۔ سرمایہ کاری: Investment

بینک بہت سی کمپنیوں کے حصص (Shares) اور سرکاری کفالتیں خرید لیتا ہے۔ حصص پر بینک منافع کماتا ہے جبکہ کفالتوں پر سود ملتا ہے۔ یہ رقم بینک کی آمدنی کا بڑا ذریعہ بنتی ہے۔

6۔ قیمتی اشیاء کا محافظ: Cutodian of Valuables

بینک لاکرز کی سہولت مہیا کرتے ہیں جہاں لوگ اپنی قیمتی دستاویزات مثلاً وصیت نامے، جائیداد کی رجسٹریاں، اور دیگر قیمتی اشیاء مثلاً زیورات اور پرائز بونڈ وغیرہ محفوظ کر لیتے ہیں۔ بینک اس کے عوض معمولی چارجز وصول کرتا ہے۔

7۔ خدمات بطور ایجنٹ:

بینک اپنے گاہکوں کے لیے بطور ایجنٹ کام کرتا ہے مثلاً اُن کی طرف سے کرایہ، ٹیکس اور بیمہ وغیرہ کی قسط ادا کرتا ہے اور دوسری طرف وصول ہونے والی رقمیں اُن کے اکاؤنٹ میں منتقل کرتا ہے۔ جیسے بجلی، گیس اور پانی کے بل وغیرہ کی رقوم متعلقہ محکموں کے اکاؤنٹ میں منتقل کرتا ہے۔
